cards.q: The three kinds of prophethood
cards.a: (1) Law-bearing prophethood (tashri’i) — bringing a new law: ended with the Holy Prophet (sa). (2) Independent non-law-bearing prophethood (mustaqil) — received directly, not through following an earlier prophet, like Aaron or Yahya: also ended, since no one can now reach Allah except through the Holy Prophet (sa). (3) Prophethood by reflection (zilli/ummati) — granted only through perfect obedience to the Holy Prophet (sa) and as his reflection: this remains open. Opponents believe all three are closed — yet expect the independent Israelite prophet Jesus to return.
cards.x:
Prophethood is of three kinds.

First, law-bearing (tashri’i): a prophet who brings a new law. This ended with the Holy Prophet (sa).

Second, independent non-law-bearing (mustaqil): a prophet who receives prophethood directly, not through following an earlier prophet — like Aaron or Yahya. This has also ended, because no one can now reach Allah except through the Holy Prophet (sa).

Third, prophethood by reflection (zilli or ummati): granted only through perfect obedience to the Holy Prophet (sa), as his reflection. This remains open.

The Promised Messiah (as) wrote that no spiritual excellence can now be reached without the Holy Prophet’s (sa) seal. Opponents say all three are closed — yet they expect Jesus, an independent Israelite prophet, to return.

cards.a: The Holy Prophet (sa) is like the sun whose light lasts until the Day of Judgement. In Arabic and Urdu, “last” is often used to mean the most perfect of its kind.

cards.q: Why the life or death of Jesus is such an important question
cards.a: Three reasons: (1) Christianity — most of the world’s religion — rests on Jesus being alive in heaven as God’s son; his death breaks its foundation. (2) Many Muslims, influenced by Christian ideas, believe he is alive in heaven, which raises him above the Holy Prophet (sa). (3) No one will consider the Promised Messiah’s claim seriously until it is clear that Jesus of Nazareth has died.

Third, no one will consider the claim of the Promised Messiah (as) seriously until it is clear that Jesus of Nazareth has died. The Quran asks: if you die, shall they live on for ever (21:35)? Opening with these three reasons shows why the question matters.

cards.q: Why does the Quran say both “they did not kill him” and “nor crucify him”?
cards.a: Because the Jews’ claim was specifically that they had killed him by crucifixion — the death the Torah calls “accursed” — to prove he was a false prophet. The Quran denies both the killing and the accursed death on the cross; it does not deny that he was put on the cross.
cards.x:
Verse 4:158 says the Jews did not kill Jesus (as) and did not crucify him. Why mention both?

Because the Jews’ claim was specific: they had killed him by crucifixion. The Torah says “he that is hanged is accursed of God” (Deuteronomy 21:23). Death on the cross would therefore prove, in their eyes, that he was a false prophet under God’s curse.

The Quran denies both the killing and the accursed death on the cross. It does not deny that he was put on the cross. This clears his name and fits the account that he was taken down alive.

cards.q: Grammar of “shubbiha lahum” — no one else was made to look like him
cards.a: شُبِّهَ is a past passive verb. If it meant “someone was made to resemble Jesus”, the Arabic would need the person resembling him as the subject — but no such person is mentioned anywhere in the verse. Its subject is the matter itself: “it was made doubtful/obscure to them.” Also, punishing an innocent look-alike would be unjust.
cards.x:
The verse says “shubbiha lahum” — it was made to appear so to them. Shubbiha is a past passive verb.

If it meant that someone else was made to look like Jesus (as), that person would have to be mentioned as the subject. No such person is mentioned anywhere in the verse. The subject is the matter itself: the event was made doubtful or obscure to them. The verse goes on to say that those who differ about it are in doubt.

There is also a moral problem: punishing an innocent look-alike in his place would be unjust, and Allah is not unjust. Point to the grammar first — no one else is named.

cards.a: When ‘Abdullah b. ‘Amr (Jabir’s father) was martyred at Uhud, Allah asked him what he wished; he asked to be sent back to the world to be martyred again. cards.a: There was no such belief among the Companions — they agreed all earlier prophets had died (3:145). cards.q: “Every one of the People of the Book will believe in him before his death” (4:160)
cards.a: This verse cannot mean all Jews and Christians will believe in Jesus when he returns: millions have already died without believing, and hadith say thousands of Jews will follow the Dajjal. It means every one of them holds a belief about his (supposed) death on the cross before their own death.
cards.x:
• “In min… illa” is a restriction covering every individual. If the opponents’ meaning were right, Allah would have had to keep every Jew alive until Jesus’ return.
• Hadith: 70,000 Jews from Isfahan will be with the Dajjal (Kanz al-Ummal) — they clearly will not all believe.
• The pronoun in بِهِ can refer to “we killed the Messiah” (4:158): every Jew believes he was killed on the cross, and every Christian too, since their whole creed rests on it.
• Imam Nawawi (Sharh Muslim) said most commentators referred قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ to the Kitabi’s death (see site page).

cards.q: “He will speak to people in the cradle and in middle age (kahlan)” (3:47)
cards.a: Opponents say Jesus was raised at 33, so he must return to speak in middle age. But kahl begins around thirty, and according to authentic narrations he lived to 120 — so he spoke in middle age long ago.
cards.x:
Verse 3:47 says Jesus (as) would speak to people in the cradle and in middle age (kahlan). Some argue that because he was raised at about 33, he must come back to speak in middle age.

But kahl, middle age, begins around the age of thirty. And according to narrations, Jesus lived to about 120. So he spoke to people in middle age long ago, during his life on earth.

There is no need for him to return to fulfil this verse.

cards.q: “I will purify you from the disbelievers” — doesn’t being on the cross contradict it?
cards.a: Purification (tathir) means clearing him of the disbelievers’ accusations, not that he was never touched. The Quran uses the same word for the Prophet’s household, who certainly faced hardship.
cards.x:
In 3:56 Allah promises Jesus (as): “I will clear you of those who disbelieve.” Some ask how this fits with him being put on the cross.

Purification (tathir) here means clearing his name of the false charges of the disbelievers — not that he would never be touched. The Quran uses the same word for the household of the Holy Prophet (sa) in 33:34, who certainly faced hardships.

The Holy Prophet (sa) was wounded at Uhud, and that did not make him any less honoured. In the same way, Allah cleared Jesus of the accusation of an accursed death.

cards.a: The words “from heaven” in Bayhaqi’s narration of the descent are not in the version Imam Suyuti quoted from Bayhaqi, and the narrator Yunus b. Yazid is criticised for weak memory and tadlis. They are a later addition.
cards.x: The handwritten copy of Bayhaqi was first printed in 1328 AH — after the claim of the Promised Messiah (as). The authentic versions in Bukhari and Muslim say only “when the son of Mary descends among you” — no “from heaven”.

cards.q: Narrations “Jesus did not die” and “death will come to Jesus”
cards.a: The narration “inna ‘Isa lam yamut” is mursal (from Hasan Basri, not the Prophet sa), and four of its five narrators are weak; one is Rabi’ b. Anas, whose narrations via Abu Ja’far are rejected by the hadith critics.
cards.x:
Some quote a narration that “Jesus has not died”. It is found in Ibn Jarir’s commentary as a mursal report from Hasan Basri — it does not go back to the Holy Prophet (sa).

Its chain is weak. One of its narrators is Rabi’ b. Anas; Ibn Hajar notes in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib that hadith critics avoid his narrations through Abu Ja’far because they contain much confusion.

A weak, unconnected report cannot override clear Quranic verses such as 3:145 and 5:118. Ask for the chain of narration.

cards.q: “I am the Black Stone” — dreams about the Ka’bah stone
cards.a: This was a dream in which someone kissed his feet and he said “I am the Black Stone.” He explained it himself: the Black Stone is a sign of blessing that people kiss for Allah’s sake; in the same way, Allah placed blessing in him for the people of this age. Dreams are interpreted; prophets and saints had similar dreams.
cards.x:
This refers to a dream. In it, someone kissed his feet, and he said “I am the Black Stone.”

The Promised Messiah (as) explained the dream himself. The Black Stone is a sign of blessing that people kiss for Allah’s sake. In the same way, Allah placed blessing in him for the people of this age.

Dreams are interpreted, not taken literally. The Quran records Yusuf’s dream of the sun, moon and stars bowing to him (12:5) — no one takes that literally either.

cards.q: Revelations in English and other languages — and grammar objections
cards.a: Revelation meant for other nations can come in their languages: Solomon understood the speech of birds; the Quran contains non-Arabic words. Grammar objections to the English revelations (e.g. “exchange” used for “change”) ignore that God’s word is not bound by a grammar book — and the Quran itself switches person and tense (iltifat) in ways grammarians once called errors.
cards.x: Abrupt change from third to second person within one sentence is a known Quranic style (e.g. Al-Fatiha: “Praise to Allah… You alone we worship”). Such objections were also raised against the Quran by its critics.

cards.q: “Tichi Tichi” and the angel’s name — strange words in revelations
cards.a: There is no revelation “Tichi Tichi”; he saw in a dream a man who looked like an angel, who, when asked his name, gave a descriptive name (“Tichi” — one who comes at the right time to help) instead of a personal name. Angels in the Quran and Hadith also appear in human form with descriptive names.
cards.x:
The allegation quotes a “revelation” of “Tichi Tichi”. There is no such revelation.

What he described was a dream in which he saw a man who looked like an angel. When asked his name, the angel gave a descriptive name — “Tichi”, meaning one who comes at the right time to help — rather than a personal name.

Angels appear in human form in the Quran, as with Mary (19:18), and in the Hadith. Correct the quotation first, then explain the dream.

cards.q: “He received satanic revelations” / “He misunderstood some revelations”
cards.a: Prophets sometimes interpret a revelation’s details by their own judgement and may later learn a fuller meaning — Noah thought his son was of his family (11:46–47); the Holy Prophet (sa) was shown Laylat al-Qadr and then made to forget its date (Bukhari); he saw in a dream that he would perform Umrah, and set out in the year of Hudaybiyyah. This does not make the revelation false. Satan’s whispers are erased by Allah, who makes His signs firm (22:53).
cards.x: The Promised Messiah (as) wrote that prophets are infallible in conveying revelation, but in interpreting it by ijtihad they can err, as Noah did. He reported once hearing an impure voice after a revelation and recognised it as satanic — proof he distinguished them.

cards.q: Revelations “Eli Eli lima sabaqtani”, “Hosh’ana Nas’a” and “I was given power to give life and death”
cards.a: These Hebrew/Aramaic phrases are the words of Jesus and a prayer: “Eli Eli lima sabaqtani” — my God, why have you forsaken me — expressed his trial; “Hosanna, na’sa” means “save, we pray — granted”. The power “to give death and life” refers to spiritual life and death and to prophecies of destruction for enemies, by God’s permission — as Jesus revived the dead spiritually.
cards.x:
Some revelations contain Hebrew or Aramaic words, which opponents mock.

“Eli Eli lima sabaqtani” — “My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?” — are the words of Jesus on the cross; they expressed a trial he faced. “Hosanna, na’sa” means “save, we pray” — the word used for Jesus in Matthew 21:9.

The revelation about being given power “to give life and death” refers to spiritual life and death, and to warning prophecies about enemies, all by Allah’s permission — just as Jesus said he raised the dead “by Allah’s leave” (3:50). Translating the words usually removes the objection.

cards.q: Dr Abdul Hakim’s prophecy that the Promised Messiah would die by 4 August 1908
cards.a: The apostate Dr Abdul Hakim kept changing his prophecy (first 3 years, then 14 months, then 4 August 1908). Before that, the Promised Messiah (as) had published that his own death was near (Al-Wasiyyat, Dec. 1905). He replied that Allah would seize Abdul Hakim and that his opponents’ prophecy would be proved false. He died on 26 May 1908 — not on Abdul Hakim’s date.
cards.x: A prophecy that keeps changing its date is self-refuting. The Promised Messiah’s death had been foretold by his own revelations; Abdul Hakim’s final date was not fulfilled.

cards.q: Prophecy about his own age (about 80 years)
cards.a: Allah told him he would live around eighty years, “a few years less or more”. Different recorded birth dates give him an age of about 74–75 (lunar years more). Since the revelation itself allowed “a few years less”, it was fulfilled. Opponents ask how he could know his age without a certain birth date — the revelation gave an approximate span, not an exact count.
cards.x: His birth is generally given as 13 February 1835 (14 Shawwal 1250 AH); he died 26 May 1908 (1326 AH): about 73 solar / 76 lunar years — within “a few years less”.

cards.q: Abdullah Atham’s prophecy
cards.a: After a 15-day debate in 1893, the prophecy said the party in the wrong would fall into “hawiyah” (abyss) within 15 months unless he turned to the truth. Atham showed great fear, stopped writing against Islam, and was in terror; when challenged to swear that he had not turned to the truth, with a reward offered up to 4,000 rupees, he refused. He died in July 1896, shortly after the extended warning.
cards.x: Atham excused himself saying Christians may not swear oaths (Matthew 5:34) — but Paul repeatedly took oaths in God’s name (Galatians 1:20; 2 Corinthians 1:23), and Hebrews 6:16 calls an oath the end of all dispute. His refusal showed he had inwardly turned.

cards.q: Prophecy of a son to Manzur Muhammad (“Bashir al-Daula”, “‘Alam Kabab”)
cards.a: In a vision (19 February 1906) he was told Manzur Muhammad would have a son with names like Bashir al-Daula and ‘Alam Kabab. cards.q: Plague in Qadian, Batalvi’s humiliation and “nafilatan lak”
cards.a:
• Plague: the revelation promised protection of his house (“I will protect all who are in this house”) and that Qadian would be saved from the destructive, widespread plague that sweeps people away — not that no case would ever occur. Qadian was protected compared to surrounding areas.
• Muhammad Husain Batalvi, who issued the first fatwa of kufr, was humbled; he later admitted Ahmadis were Muslims in court.
• “Nafilatan lak” (a grandson as a gift): he explained it could be fulfilled through a son of Mahmud — and it was.
cards.x: “Avi” (refuge after hardship): he explained Allah gives shelter after some trial — so a few cases were not against the prophecy (Haqiqat al-Wahi).

cards.q: “He was a poet” / “He wrote false references”
cards.a:
• Poetry: the Quran rejects the poets who say what they don’t do (26:225–227), not good verse; the Prophet (sa) praised wise poetry and had Hassan b. Thabit as poet. His poems are praise of God and the Prophet (sa).
• Wrong references: most alleged “false references” are from editions that differ, or Christian changes in the Bible across editions; some are slips of memory, like the Prophet (sa) praying two rak’ahs in Zuhr by mistake (Dhul-Yadayn hadith) — a slip is not a lie. E.g. he cited Tafsir Mazhari of Thanaullah Panipati, which opponents confuse with Thanaullah Amritsari.
cards.x: Bukhari cited with “min al-sama’”: he never claimed those words were in Bukhari; opponents themselves have quoted Bayhaqi with wrong attributions. Always check the original book and context.

cards.q: Contradictions in his writings (prophethood claim and denial, etc.)
cards.a: Apparent contradictions arise when the same word is used in two senses. When he denied being a “nabi”, he denied being a law-bearing or independent prophet; when he affirmed it, he meant a prophet by reflection (zilli/ummati) without new law. The Quran itself appears to contradict on the surface (e.g. “no compulsion in religion” and “strive against the disbelievers”), which context resolves.
cards.x: Other alleged contradictions (e.g. whether he learned from a teacher, the 5 prayers “equal to 50” — from Bukhari’s Mi’raj hadith, the 400 prophets of Ahab — 1 Kings 22) each have straightforward answers in context. He stated on oath that he learned the Quran and Hadith from no human teacher in the sense of the Mahdi’s learning (Ayyam al-Sulh).

cards.q: Harsh language — “dhurriyyat al-baghaya”, “jungle pigs”
cards.a: His strong words were in reply to opponents who used vile abuse, and they follow the style of the Quran and Hadith, which use strong words for the wicked (e.g. “cattle”, “dogs” 7:177, “zanim” 68:14). “Dhurriyyat al-baghaya” in Arabic means rebellious, disobedient people — not literally children of prostitutes, as Arabic lexicons and usage show. He never abused anyone in the sense of foul language.
cards.x: The Holy Prophet (sa) also said a time will come when only the name of Islam remains, and the ‘ulama will be the worst under the sky (Mishkat). Strong words about corrupt scholars are hadith language.

cards.q: Hadith of plague, Mubarak Ahmad’s death, “kana fil-Hind nabiyyan”
cards.a:
• Leaving a city in plague: he told people not to flee from plague areas, following the hadith; his own guidance matched it.
• Mubarak Ahmad: his death in childhood had been foretold at his birth (“I will fall from Allah and be struck”, Tiryaq al-Qulub) — so it fulfilled a prophecy.
• “There was a prophet in India, black in colour, named Kahin”: he quoted it from an earlier collection of narrations (as the Pocket Book shows) as an indication that prophets came to India; it is not his invention.
cards.x:
Three short points.

Plague: he told people not to flee from places struck by plague. This matched the hadith in Bukhari: do not enter a land with plague, and do not leave it if it breaks out where you are.

Mubarak Ahmad: his son’s early death had been foretold at his birth (Tiryaq al-Qulub), so it fulfilled a prophecy rather than contradicting one.

“There was a prophet in India”: he quoted this from an earlier collection of narrations, as the Pocket Book shows, as an indication that prophets came to India. It was not his invention.

cards.q: Did he claim to be superior to the Holy Prophet (sa)?
cards.a: No. He called himself the servant (ghulam) of the Holy Prophet (sa) and said everything he had came through him. Statements like “I am Adam, I am Noah, I am Muhammad and Ahmad” are buruz (spiritual reflection): the Mahdi is to show the qualities of all prophets. Even Shia books say the Mahdi will announce “whoever wants to see Muhammad, here I am”. Numbers of signs shown to him are counted as signs of the Holy Prophet (sa).
cards.x:
He never claimed to be superior to the Holy Prophet (sa). He called himself the Holy Prophet’s servant (ghulam) and said that everything he received came through him. In a Persian verse he wrote: “After God, I am drunk with love of Muhammad; if this is disbelief, by God I am the greatest disbeliever.”

Statements such as “I am Adam, I am Noah, I am Muhammad and Ahmad” are buruz — spiritual reflection. The Mahdi was to show the qualities of all the prophets. Even a Shia source, Bihar al-Anwar, says the Mahdi will announce: whoever wants to see Muhammad, here I am.

The signs shown to him are counted as signs of the Holy Prophet (sa).

cards.q: Signs of the Mahdi: from Fatima’s progeny, born in Makkah, named Muhammad, bringing law?
cards.a: The narrations themselves disagree: some say the Mahdi is from Hasan’s line, some Husain’s, some Abbas’s; his birthplace is given as Madinah, Makkah, the West or Khurasan. Such contradictions show these details are not certain. The strong hadith say only “la Mahdi illa ‘Isa” and “your Imam from among you”. He has spiritual kinship with the Prophet’s family, and the name Ahmad/Ghulam Ahmad.
cards.x:
Opponents say the Mahdi must be from Fatima’s descendants, born in Makkah, named Muhammad, and so on. The narrations themselves disagree on these details.

Some say the Mahdi is from Hasan’s line, some Husain’s, some Abbas’s. His birthplace is given variously as Madinah, Makkah, the West or Khurasan. Nawab Siddiq Hasan Khan recorded these differences. Such contradictions show these details are not certain.

The stronger narrations say “there is no Mahdi except Jesus” and “your Imam from among you”. The Holy Prophet (sa) also said Salman the Persian is “from us, the people of the house”, showing a spiritual kinship with his family.

cards.q: “He studied under teachers” / “He never performed Hajj”
cards.a:
• Teachers: he learned basic books as a boy; his claim was that he learned the knowledge of the Quran from no human — Moses too sought knowledge from Khidr. Imam Nawawi says even a great scholar should learn from one more knowledgeable.
• Hajj: Hajj is obligatory only when the route is safe and one is able (3:98); fatwas of death were issued against him in the Hijaz. The hadith of the Messiah performing Hajj is a vision (kashf) — in the same vision the Prophet (sa) saw the Dajjal circumambulating the Ka’bah, which shows it must be interpreted.
cards.x:
Two objections.

Teachers: as a boy he learned basic books from teachers, which he never denied. His claim was that he learned the knowledge of the Quran from Allah, not from any human. Moses (as) too sought knowledge from Khidr.

Hajj: Hajj is a duty only for those who can find a safe way to it (3:98). Fatwas of death had been issued against him in the Hijaz, so the route was not safe. The hadith of the Messiah performing Hajj describes a vision; in the same vision the Holy Prophet (sa) saw the Dajjal going round the Ka’bah, which shows it must be interpreted (Muslim).

cards.q: Illness (“miraq”), medicines, silk and musk
cards.a: The hadith says the Messiah will descend “between two yellow sheets” — interpreted as two illnesses — and that he would have headaches/dizziness. Illness is no fault: prophets were tested with illness (Job). Medicines with alcohol content or silk for illness are allowed by need: the Prophet (sa) permitted Zubair and ‘Abd al-Rahman to wear silk because of an itch.
cards.x: “Miraq” is distorted by opponents into madness; he described only physical weakness and headaches. A man who wrote more than 80 books and led a movement was clearly of sound mind.

cards.q: Purdah, breaking the fast while travelling, Bahishti Maqbara
cards.a:
• Purdah: he followed Islamic purdah; visiting women relatives or elderly women in a proper manner is in the Sunnah — the Prophet (sa) visited Umm Haram, who served him food.
• Fasting: breaking the fast on a journey is the Quran’s permission (2:185) and the Prophet (sa) did it at ‘Usfan in Ramadan.
• Bahishti Maqbara: not “buying paradise” — it is for those who sacrifice part of their wealth and live righteously, after Allah’s promise of paradise for believers who strive with their wealth (61:11–12).
cards.x:
Three objections answered from the Quran and Sunnah.

Purdah: he followed Islamic purdah. Visiting women relatives or elderly women in a proper way is in the Sunnah — the Holy Prophet (sa) visited Umm Haram, who served him food.

Fasting while travelling: the Quran allows it (2:185), and the Holy Prophet (sa) broke his fast publicly at ‘Usfan during Ramadan (Bukhari).

Bahishti Maqbara: it is not buying paradise. It is for those who sacrifice part of their wealth and live righteous lives, following Allah’s promise to believers who strive with their wealth and their persons (61:11–12).

cards.q: Objections about his death, burial place and illness at death
cards.a: Opponents mock the manner of his death (cholera allegation, diarrhoea). Illness at death is no sign of falsehood: saints like Abdul Qadir Jilani suffered severe diarrhoea; the Prophet (sa) suffered severe fever. “A prophet is buried where he dies” is a narration about the Holy Prophet (sa) only (Tirmidhi, which calls it gharib and weak).
cards.x:
Opponents mock the illness at the time of his death. Illness at death is no sign of falsehood. Saints such as Abdul Qadir Jilani suffered severe illness, and the Holy Prophet’s (sa) fever in his last illness was twice as severe as any man’s (Bukhari).

On burial: the saying “a prophet is buried where he dies” is about the Holy Prophet (sa) only. Tirmidhi himself calls it gharib, and one of its narrators is weak.

Ask: if illness at death disproved a saint, what would that say about the Holy Prophet’s (sa) severe fever?

cards.q: Takfir: “Ahmadis call other Muslims kafir”
cards.a: The fatwas of kufr began from the other side: Maulvi Muhammad Husain Batalvi and others declared him and his followers kafir first. He explained that denying a commissioned messenger is “kufr” in the sense of rejecting a divine messenger, not expulsion from the Ummah of the Holy Prophet (sa). Meanwhile the various sects have issued fatwas of kufr against each other — Deobandis, Barelvis, Ahl-e-Hadith, Shias — and even against Sir Syed and Quaid-e-Azam.
cards.x:
The fatwas of kufr began from the other side. Maulvi Muhammad Husain Batalvi and others declared the Promised Messiah (as) and his followers kafir first. The Holy Prophet (sa) warned that whoever calls his brother a kafir, it returns to one of them (Bukhari).

The Promised Messiah (as) explained (Haqiqat al-Wahi) that denying a commissioned messenger is “kufr” in the sense of rejecting a divine messenger, not in the sense of leaving Islam.

Meanwhile, many sects have issued fatwas of kufr against one another — Deobandis, Barelvis, Ahl-e-Hadith and Shias — and some even against Sir Syed and Quaid-e-Azam. Ask who issued the first fatwa.

cards.q: Non-Ahmadi scholars’ slanders against the prophets
cards.a: Ahmadis uphold the innocence of all prophets. Some non-Ahmadi commentators repeat stories that Ibrahim told three lies, Adam committed shirk, Yusuf intended sin, Dawud coveted Uriah’s wife, Sulaiman lost his kingdom to a demon. The Promised Messiah (as) explained these narrations in a way that preserves prophetic purity — e.g. Ibrahim’s “lies” were figures of speech (tawriyah), not lies.
cards.x:
Ahmadis uphold the innocence of all prophets. Some non-Ahmadi commentators repeat stories that Ibrahim told three lies, Adam committed shirk, Yusuf intended sin, Dawud coveted Uriah’s wife, and Sulaiman lost his kingdom to a demon.

The Promised Messiah (as) explained such narrations in a way that keeps the prophets pure. For example, Ibrahim’s so-called lies were statements with a hidden true meaning (tawriyah), not lies — the Quran calls him “a truthful man and a prophet” (19:42).

This shows who truly honours the prophets.

cards.q: Are the Vedas a universal, complete revelation? (Arya Samaj)
cards.a: The Quran presents a complete teaching for all mankind and challenges anyone to produce its like (17:89). The Vedas, by the Arya Samaj’s own account, were given to four rishis, are restricted in language and caste, contain disputed contents (even the number of Vedas — three or four), and their teaching about God and rituals is not suited to all people or ages.
cards.x: The Pocket Book lists Arya Samaj sources (Satyarth Prakash of Swami Dayanand) on the Vedas, their contents and rituals, and shows internal disagreement.

cards.q: Niyoga in Arya Samaj teaching
cards.a: Satyarth Prakash (ch. 4) permits niyoga — a married woman having children with another man under certain conditions. Islam regards this as against human nature and modesty; it shows the teaching cannot be a perfect divine law.
cards.x:
Swami Dayanand’s Satyarth Prakash (chapter 4) permits niyoga: under certain conditions, a married woman may have children with a man other than her husband, and the relationship ends once that purpose is fulfilled.

Islam regards this as against human nature, modesty and the dignity of marriage. A teaching that allows it cannot be a perfect divine law.

Raise this only with Arya Samaj debaters who attack Islamic marriage, and quote the book calmly.

cards.q: Are soul and matter eternal (uncreated)?
cards.a: If soul and matter are eternal and self-existing like God, God is not their Creator and not truly needed; their joining and separating would also be eternal properties, needing no God. Islam teaches that Allah alone is eternal and everything else is created by Him.
cards.x:
Arya Samaj teaches that soul and matter are eternal and uncreated, like God.

If soul and matter exist by themselves from eternity, then God did not create them and is not truly needed for their existence. Their joining and separating could also be their own eternal properties, needing no God.

Islam teaches that Allah alone is eternal: His is the creation and the command (7:55), and He is the First and the Last (57:4). Ask: if soul and matter are eternal and uncaused like God, what makes God God?

cards.q: Questions on transmigration of souls (reincarnation)
cards.a: If every difference among creatures is punishment for deeds in a past life, then: what deed earned the first birth? Why does no one remember their past life to reform? Why is the earth, plants and food — which existed before humans — a reward for anything? The Pocket Book lists forty such questions.
cards.x:
The doctrine of transmigration says every difference among creatures is punishment or reward for deeds in a past life.

This raises questions. What deed earned the very first birth? Why does no one remember their past life, so they could learn and reform? The earth, plants and food existed before humans — what deeds were they a reward for? The Pocket Book lists forty such questions.

The Quran’s principle is that no one bears another’s burden (6:165). Usually one question is enough: what deed earned the first birth?

cards.q: The Promised Messiah in Hindu scriptures (Kalki avatar)
cards.a: Krishna said in the Gita: whenever righteousness declines, I appear (as an avatar) to protect the good and re-establish dharma. The Mahabharata describes the dark age (Kaliyug) — falsehood, greed, quarrels — after which the Kalki avatar appears with spiritual power to revive dharma. The Promised Messiah (as) claimed to be this awaited reformer for Hindus.
cards.x: The Arya Samaj founder himself said revelation was given to rishis because they were the purest — by that standard the Promised Messiah’s (as) pure life is a proof (he challenged anyone to point to a flaw in his life).

cards.q: Was Baba Guru Nanak a Muslim saint?
cards.a: Ahmadis believe Baba Nanak was a Muslim wali (friend of God), based on the Promised Messiah’s (as) research and a vision. Sikh sources show Muslims called him “Nanak Shah”, he offered the five daily prayers, condemned those who abandon prayer, went on Hajj to Makkah, praised the Quran, and his relic cloak (chola) at Dera Baba Nanak bears Quranic verses including the Kalima.
cards.x: Muslim lands have places named after him as a qalandar/wali (Sikh historians, e.g. Gyani Gyan Singh, Tawarikh Guru Khalsa). The Promised Messiah’s (as) book Sat Bachan (1895) presents this evidence.

cards.q: The awaited Guru / “Nihkalank” avatar in Sikh writings
cards.a: Sikh scriptures and Janam Sakhis speak of an avatar to come in the dark age: “Nihkalank” (the spotless one), and in some places say he will be a Muslim. cards.x: Ahmadis present the Promised Messiah (as) — from Qadian in district Gurdaspur, near Batala — as the fulfilment of these prophecies of a great reformer for all religions.

cards.q: Baha’i faith: Baha’ullah’s claims
cards.a: Baha’ullah claimed that he himself sent down revelation (a claim to divinity), declared the Shariah of Muhammad (sa) abrogated by the laws of the Bab and himself, issued rulings of disbelief against those who reject him, and his followers treat his shrine as a place of prostration. Ahmadis, by contrast, hold the Holy Prophet’s (sa) law as final and unchanged.
cards.x: Baha’is practise taqiyya-like concealment, presenting themselves as Muslims to the public. Their books (Bahr al-‘Irfan, Nuqtat al-Kaf) describe the “lesser resurrection” as the Bab’s appearance and the “greater resurrection” as Baha’ullah’s.

cards.q: The faith of the first three Caliphs according to the Quran
cards.a: Allah declared His pleasure with those who pledged allegiance under the tree at Hudaybiyyah — Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman among them. The verse of Istikhlaf promises successors who establish the religion and turn fear into security — fulfilled by the first Caliphs.
cards.x:
The Quran itself speaks of the faith of the first three Caliphs.

Allah declared His pleasure with the believers who pledged allegiance under the tree at Hudaybiyyah (48:19) — Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman were among them. Verse 9:40 describes Abu Bakr as the “second of the two” in the cave, to whom the Holy Prophet (sa) said: “Grieve not, Allah is with us.”

The verse of Istikhlaf (24:56) promises believers successors who would establish the religion and change fear into security — fulfilled by the early Caliphs.

Nahj al-Balagha, the collection of Hazrat Ali’s sermons and letters valued by Shias, praises the early Caliphs.

cards.q: Common Shia objections: Ghadir “mawla”, Fadak, fleeing in battle, Hadith al-Qirtas
cards.a:
• “Man kuntu mawlahu fa-Aliyyun mawlahu”: mawla here means friend/beloved — whoever loves me, Ali loves him; if it meant appointment as Caliph, the 124,000 Companions would not have elected Abu Bakr months later.
• Abu Bakr and Umar fleeing at Uhud: false — Tabari records them standing with the Prophet (sa) in the pass.
• Fadak: the Prophet (sa) said “We prophets leave no inheritance; what we leave is charity” (Bukhari); Abu Bakr followed this.
• Hadith al-Qirtas (the pen and paper): the Prophet (sa) left the Book of Allah (Muslim) — no essential instruction was lost.
cards.x:
Common Shia objections, briefly.

Ghadir — “whoever’s mawla I am, Ali is his mawla”: mawla here means friend and beloved. If it were an appointment as Caliph, the Companions would not have elected Abu Bakr months later, and Ali would not have pledged to him.

Fleeing at Uhud: Tarikh al-Tabari records Abu Bakr and Umar standing with the Holy Prophet (sa) in the mountain pass.

Fadak: the Holy Prophet (sa) said prophets leave no inheritance; what they leave is charity (Bukhari). Abu Bakr followed this.

The pen and paper (Qirtas): the Holy Prophet (sa) left the Book of Allah; no essential instruction was lost. Take one objection at a time.

cards.q: Taqiyya and Mut’ah
cards.a:
• Taqiyya (concealing faith): Hazrat Ali never practised it — he did not hide his views or fight the first Caliphs, and openly kept his faith even in Makkah when danger was greatest. A religion of concealment cannot be preached.
• Mut’ah (temporary marriage): the Prophet (sa) announced it forbidden until the Day of Judgement; Ali himself married many times and never contracted mut’ah.
cards.x:
Taqiyya — concealing one’s faith: Hazrat Ali did not hide his beliefs. He kept his faith openly even in Makkah when danger was greatest, and he did not fight the first Caliphs. A religion built on concealment cannot be preached openly.

Mut’ah — temporary marriage: the Holy Prophet (sa) declared it forbidden until the Day of Resurrection (Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Nikah). Hazrat Ali married many times and is not known to have contracted mut’ah.

The simplest point to make is that Ali himself never practised taqiyya.

"I said nothing to them except that which Thou didst command me- worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.`And I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them, but since Thou didst cause me to die, Thou hast been t
cards.x:
These verses describe a conversation on the Day of Judgement. Allah asks Jesus (as) whether he told people to take him and his mother as gods. Jesus replies that he only taught what he was commanded, and that he was a witness over his people only while he was among them; “but since You caused me to die (tawaffaitani), You have been the Watcher over them.”

So Jesus says he did not know what his followers did after his death. The false belief in his divinity arose after tawaffa — after his death. If he had returned to the world, he would know. The scan shows the original page.

cards.q: Explanation of  tawaffaitani from “Sahi Bukhari”
cards.a: Hazrat Ibn Abbas, Allah be pleased with him relates, that the Holy Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, delivered a sermon and said:- "…… O, people, a number of people from the followers of my Ummah would be taken to the hell, thereupon, I shall say, O my Lord, these are my companions. Then I would be told: you do not know what they contrived after you. At that time, I shall say precisely what the righteous servant- Jesus son of Mary- said: "And I was witness over them as long as I remained among them, but since Thou didst cause me to die, Thou hast been the watcher over them."
cards.x:
In this hadith of Bukhari, the Holy Prophet (sa) says that on the Day of Judgement some people of his Ummah will be taken away, and he will say what “the righteous servant” said: “I was a witness over them while I was among them, but when You caused me to die (tawaffaitani)…”

The Holy Prophet (sa) used the very words of Jesus (as) from 5:118 about himself. For the Holy Prophet (sa), tawaffaitani clearly means his death. The same words cannot mean death for him and being lifted alive for Jesus.

Ibn Taymiyya explains that, by Allah’s law, the moon can only be eclipsed on the nights when it is full — the 13th, 14th and 15th of the lunar month — and the sun only on the days when the moon is hidden — the 27th, 28th and 29th.

This helps explain the hadith of the eclipses: “the first night” of the moon’s eclipse nights is the 13th, and “the middle day” of the sun’s is the 28th — exactly when the eclipses of Ramadan 1894 took place.

cards.q: Blessings of Khatm-e-Nabuwwat The Ahmadiyya-Community and blessings of Khatam-e-Nabuwwat
cards.a: Khatm-e-Nubuwwat One of the accusations levelled on the Ahmadiya Muslim Jamaat, among many others is that Jamaat Ahmadiya does not accept the Holy Prophet Muhammad s.a.s.
cards.x:
as Khatam-un-Nabiyyin and has adopted a new doctrine which deviates from that of the ummat of the past 1300 years in this mater. Like many other unfounded allegations this one is also wrong and baseless. The reality is that the strength of conviction with which Jamaat Ahmadiyya accepts the Holy Prophet (pbuh) as khatam-un-Nabiyyin is unparalled. The Founder of the Ahmadiyya Jamaat says:

"It is alleged that I and my Jamma't do not accept the Holy prophet (pbuh) as khatam-un-Nabiyin. This is a great lie upon us. The strength, certainity, and full understanding with which we believe in the Holy Prophet (pbuh) to be khatam-un- nabiyin and accept him as such, others do not believe even in a hundred thousandth part of it". (AlHakam 17 Marc 1905)

When the Promised Messiah a.s. is quoted to the opponents, they try to give the false impression that this acceptance is only a lip service. According to them the Promised Messiah has opened the door of a new kind of prophethood, and whatever he calls it ummati or zilli (adumberate), the rejection of khatam-e-Nabuwwat is implied. They say that the Jamaat Ahmadiyya has opened the door for the prophethood whereas past scolars of Islam considered prophethood to be absolutely finished and did not believe in any form of exception. But even minor least effort in research would show the wise that this objection too is hollow and baseless. It is a fact that the Ahmadiyya Jamaat interprets the verse Khatam-us-Nabiyyin in the same way as the holy scolars of the followers in the past and have not invented any new doctrine. The new doctrine has been invented by the opponents of Ahmadiyya themselves. To determine this mater easily we will present some statements by the learned Muslim scolars and saints taken from their famous and authentic books. These statements show their belief regarding the doctrine of Khatm -e-Nabuwwat, scans of these pasages are also being provided. Even a superficial view of these statements will show that Hazrat Massih Maud a.s. has not presented any new doctrine. He said what the learned scolars had also said in the past. In the presence of these statements there is no need for further elaboration. It will be apparent to every just reader himself. Please consider these things with a fair and God fearing mind.

Ibn Arabi wrote in Al-Futuhat al-Makkiyyah that the prophethood which ended with the Holy Prophet (sa) is law-bearing prophethood, not prophethood itself. This is the meaning of the saying that messengership and prophethood have ended: no new law-giver will come.

In the long hadith of al-Nawwas b. Sam’an in Sahih Muslim, the Holy Prophet (sa) calls the coming Messiah “Isa, the Prophet of Allah” four times.

So the Holy Prophet (sa) himself said a prophet would come after him. The question is only what kind: a follower-prophet from the Ummah, as Ahmadis believe.

cards.a: According to us, it means that prophethood manifested itself in its full and complete manner in the Holy Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him . His heart became a vessel for the complete perfection of prophethood an d then hisheart was sealed. How can the glory and superiority of Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, be manifested if we claim that he was the last to appear in the world. This is, no doubt, an interpretation of the foolish and the ignorant.
cards.x:
Hakim Tirmidhi, in Kitab Khatm al-Awliya, explains that Khatam an-Nabiyyin means prophethood appeared in the Holy Prophet (sa) in its full and complete form, and his heart was sealed with it. He asks how merely coming last could be a mark of glory.

cards.q: Divinity: Jesus Presented As God
cards.a:
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with
God and the Word was God. The same was in the
beginning with God. JOHN 1.1 / 2
cards.x:
John 1:1 — “the Word was God” — is the verse most often quoted for the divinity of Jesus.

The Pocket Book of Biblical References answers it with other verses: the Bible uses “god” for Moses (Exodus 7:1), for judges (Psalm 82:6) and even for Satan (2 Corinthians 4:4). A word like “god” used in a book does not by itself make the person God.

cards.q: Divinity: Interpolation
cards.a:
Alpha and Omega in REVELATION 1.11 does not find
support in older Greek manuscripts including the Alexanderine,
Sinaitic or Codex Ephraemis Rescriptures. (Jehovah Witness:
Aid to Bible Understanding page 56) It is now being omitted
from modern translations. (refer New English Bible: Bible
Societies)
cards.x:
Some verses used for Jesus’ divinity, such as “Alpha and Omega” in Revelation 1:11, are not found in the older Greek manuscripts (Alexandrinus, Sinaiticus, Ephraemi). Modern translations omit it.

This shows that some phrases used to prove divinity were added later. Check the version your listener uses.

mountain, and filled the whole earth. This is the dream:
and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the
king. O King, art a king of kings: for the Lord of heaven

cards.q: Argument from the New Testament
cards.a: Maulawi Muhammad Ali has quoted certain verses of the New Testament to show that when the enemies of the first Messiah accused him of blasphemy by having claimed to be the 'son of God,' the charge was rebutted by the Messiah saying that the name 'son of God' which had been given to him was only metaphorical and had been used in the same sense in which the name 'God' had been us…
cards.x:
Maulawi Muhammad Ali has quoted certain verses of the New Testament to show that when the enemies of the first Messiah accused him of blasphemy by having claimed to be the 'son of God,' the charge was rebutted by the Messiah saying that the name 'son of God' which had been given to him was only metaphorical and had been used in the same sense in which the name 'God' had been used with reference to the previous Prophets. But after the death of Jesusas, his followers began to call him the 'son of
God' in a literal sense, that is, in the same way as we understand the word 'God' to signify the Creator of the universe; and it was in this sense that the Jews accused him that he had claimed the title. From this
Maulawi Muhammad Ali proceeds to argue that just
Truth about the Split as it happened in the case of the first Messiah, even so it was necessary that it should happen, and as a matter of fact, it has actually happened, in the case of the second Messiah. His enemies accused him of having claimed to be a Prophet. This charge he denied explaining that he had been called Prophet only metaphorically. But after his death his followers, like the followers of the first Messiah, began to claim for him prophethood in the same sense in which the claim was attributed to him by his enemies. Such is
Maulawi Muhammad Ali’s reading of the parallelism.
To me, however, it seems that while Maulawi
Muhammad Ali is right in noticing a certain parallelism between the two cases, he has committed an error in the application of the parallelism.
The verses quoted from the New Testament show that the Jews charged Jesusas with having claimed to be the 'son of God' in a literal sense. Jesusas denies the charge and says that he claims to be the 'son of God' in the sense in which the previous Prophets were called 'God'. After the death of Jesusas his followers attributed to Jesus 'Godhood' in the sense implied by his enemies.
With this example before us if we turn to the case of the second Messiah, the first thing we have to
Truth about the Split inquire into is what was the charge brought against him by his enemies. We find that his enemies charged him with having claimed to be a Prophet with a new law, as will appear from the following quotations from one of his letters published in the Akhbar-e-‘Am, a daily paper of Lahore. (This is the oldest paper of the province. Its editor and proprietor are Hindu gentlemen. In this paper a report had been published to the effect that the Promised Messiahas had renounced his claim to be a Prophet. Thereupon, the
Promised Messiahas addressed a reply to the editor in his own handwriting under date the 23rd May, 1908, i.e. only 2 or 3 days before his death. A few lines from the letter are here quoted. The Promised
Messiahas wrote:
"In the Akhbar-e-‘Am of the 23rd May,
1908, in the second line of the first column, it has been reported about me, that at the dinner I pronounced a denial of my prophethood. In reference to the same, it should be known that in that meeting what I said was simply this, that I had all along been informing the public through all my writings and declare even now that the accusation, brought against me, is entirely unfounded, namely that I claim prophethood of a kind
Truth about the Split which entails severance of all my connection with Islam, which in other words means that
I claim for myself a substantive prophethood such as leaves no need for me to follow the
Holy Quran and introduces a new Kalima (formula of creed) and a new Qibla (direction to which to turn our face in prayer) and abrogates the laws of Islam and ignores the authority and example of the
Holy
Prophetsa."
While thus exonerating himself from the charges of his enemies, he proceeded in the very same letter to elucidate his own claim in the following words:
"The grounds on which I claim to be a
Prophet amount to this that I have, been vouchsafed the privilege of converse with
God, who speaks to and converses with me, answers my questions, uncovers for me things unseen, and discloses to me such secrets of the future as are not opened to any save such as are in special favour with Him.
Due to the abundance of such experiences,
He has been pleased to call me a Nabi (Prophet). Thus, I am a Nabi by virtue of the
Truth about the Split command of God and it would be a sin on my part were I to deny the fact."
Again speaking about other prophetsas he says,
"Among those favours (which they enjoyed) were prophecies and predictions in view of which those former Prophets were called Nabis." (Eik Ghalati Ka Izala).
A study of these quotations will show that the charge brought against the Promised Messiahas by his enemies was his alleged claim to be a Prophet with a new law. This charge the Promised Messiahas insistently denied. What, he said, he claimed was that he was a Nabi in the sense that knowledge of future events was frequently granted to him, and that it was in this sense that the title of Nabi had been conferred upon Prophets of old.
The above circumstances offer indeed a close parallel to those of the first Messiah, but in such a parallelism, correspondence to those followers of the first Messiah, who after his death began to call him the 'son of God' in the sense wrongly imputed to him by his enemies, was to be sought in those followers of the Promised Messiahas, who thought him to be a
Prophet with a new Law, that being the charge
Truth about the Split wrongly brought against the Promised Messiahas by his opponents. The correspondence could in no way apply to us, because we never called the Promised
Messiahas a Prophet in the sense imputed by his enemies and persistently denied by himself.

Was there then ever actually a party which believed the Promised Messiahas to be a Nabi with a new law, teaching a new creed and abrogating the
Holy Quran? On page 15 of The Split, Maulawi
Muhammad Ali has himself made mention of the actual existence of such a person. This gentleman, who calls himself an Ahmadi holds the opinion that the Islamic formula should henceforth be read as "La ilaha-Illallah Ahmad Rasuluallah". Thus Maulawi
Muhammad Ali has himself borne testimony to the fact of the actual existence of a party which holds that the Promised Messiahas was actually a Nabi in the sense imputed by his enemies and persistently denied by himself. Possessing such a knowledge, was it fair and honest on the part of Maulawi Muhammad Ali to apply the analogy to me and my party? For as a matter of fact, as I have already said, the analogy cannot apply to my party at all, but to those who regard the
Promised Messiahas as a Nabi with a new law and
Truth about the Split deem it legitimate to insert his name in the formula of the creed. But it has suited his purpose thus deliberately and intentionally to accuse me of something of which he knows me to be perfectly innocent.

cards.q: Right Application of Analogy
cards.a: Now, with regard to this remarkable gentleman (Muhammad Zahiruddin, vide pages 12-17 of The…
cards.x:
Now, with regard to this remarkable gentleman (Muhammad Zahiruddin, vide pages 12-17 of The
Split) and his relations in a certain place, he writes about me as follows: "The said Miyań Sahib (referring to me) regards the Promised Messiahas as a
Nabi and a Rasul, who brought no new law and followed the law of a previous Prophet, and shrinks from practically following the commands and prohibitions contained in the Promised Messiah’sas revelations, and refuses to regard the Promised
Messiahas, agreeably to the purport of his writings, as a Nabi and continues to persist in his mistaken views." At another place he writes: "Contrary to the opinion held by the whole of the Ahmadiyya
Community, it is my belief that the Promised
Messiahas not only made the people acknowledge him to be a Prophet without a law, but did clearly make a claim of being a Prophet with a new law." About the
Truth about the Split
Qibla, Muhammad Zahiruddin writes: "The same revelation viz".
"Adopt the seat of Abraham as thy place of prayer
"was vouchsafed also to Hadrat Mirza Sahib, (i.e. the
Promised Messiahas) the only difference being that in the Holy Quran the name 'Abraham' referred to the
Abraham who built the Kaaba whereas in the revelation of Hadrat Mirza Sahib the name referred to himself, and further that the mosque of Haram was substituted in the latter case by Qadian. Thus when he declared it illegal (for his followers) to pray behind other Muslims, the reason was not that there was any difference between their prayer and that of his own followers, nor that the Maulawis had pronounced a fatwa of heresy against him, but the underlying motive was to create a party in preparation for the ultimate change of the Qibla".
It is clear from these extracts that the writer is an exponent of the view that Hadrat Mirza Sahib was a
Prophet with a new law and had set up for his followers a new Qibla (viz. Qadian), in which direction, therefore, his followers ought to turn their faces when saying their prayers, and that they ought also to substitute his name in the formula of faith. The
Truth about the Split extracts also go to show that I and my party are opposed to him in such views. It will thus appear that the analogy which the author of The Spilt has sought to establish between my party and the followers of the first Messiah exists, if anywhere, in the party composed of the above mentioned gentleman and two or three others who share his views. As for ourselves, we believe in the prophethood of the Promised
Messiahas in the same sense in which he himself claimed the title. In the notice named Eik Ghalati Ka
Izala published by the Promised Messiahas, he says,
"In all my writings wherein I have denied being a
Nabi or a Rasul, I have done in the sense that I have not brought any new book, nor was I a new substantive Prophet. Nevertheless, as I had received spiritual blessing from my leader the Holy Prophetsa and been given his name, and been gifted by God with knowledge of future events. I was indeed a Rasul and
Nabi though without a new law. I have never denied being a Nabi of the latter kind, and since it was in this sense that I was called a Nabi and Rasul by God, I do not even now deny being called Nabi and Rasul in such a sense". We call God to witness that it is exactly in this sense that we believe in the prophethood of the
Promised Messiahas, and even our enemies, in spite of thousands of false charges which they are apt to bring
Truth about the Split against us, will not venture to deny this statement.
The case of the followers of the first Messiah was far otherwise. They did not accept him to be the "Son of
God" in the same sense in which that title was claimed by that teacher. There is, therefore, no point of resemblance between ourselves and them. We may indeed be compared to that group of men who were among the true followers of the first Messiah, whose praise has been mentioned in the Holy Quran. The misguided followers of the first Messiah may of course be compared to that section of men who believe the Promised Messiahas to be a Prophet with a new Law.
What, however, is extremely surprising to us is to see that in spite of all these facts, this last named part seems to be in special favour with Maulawi
Muhammad Ali and his friends. A common antagonism towards me seems to have served as a bond of union between them. Muhammad Zahiruddin was made a member of the advisory committee, which was formed at Lahore after the death of
Khalifatul Masih Ira. (vide the Paigham-e-Sulh of 24th
March, 1914) and his articles against me found a place in Maulawi Muhammad Ali’s magazine called the Al-Mahdi. They have since continued to have frequent interviews and Muhammad Zahiruddin
Truth about the Split reports that Maulawi Muhammad Ali once offered to employ him in the service of his Anjuman, on condition that he would not preach his views openly by notices and lectures, but he would, of course be free to ventilate them in private. But this is not all.
The Lahore Anjuman (presided over by Maulawi
Muhammad Ali) allowed Muhammad Zahiruddin on the occasion of their annual conference of 1918 to appear on their stage and to speak in support of his peculiar views. Here then is a most inexplicable paradox. Maulawi Muhammad Ali charges my party with sharing the views of Muhammad Zahiruddin. But all Zahir’s connections are with Maulawi Muhammad
Ali and Maulawi Sahib’s connections are with Zahir.
Such a union only illustrates the old adage "Birds of a feather flock together." Both of them are bent upon the destruction of the Ahmadiyya Movement. Both are, therefore, willing to act in concert, because although they differ regarding the means to be employed they both agree on their common end.
New Testament Parallel Proves the
Promised Messiahas a Prophet
Before, however, I leave this point, I think it worthwhile to point out that the verses quoted by
Maulawi Muhammad Ali from the Gospels, far from
Truth about the Split proving any resemblance between my party and those followers of Jesusas who unduly magnified his rank, furnish rather an additional proof of the prophethood of the Promised Messiahas. To further elucidate this point, I would repeat that the verses go to show that the enemies of Jesusas accused him of having 'made himself a god' (to be Son of God meant to the Jews the same as to be God). In reply Jesusas asked them whether it was not written in the Bible that they (the
Prophets) were gods. If therefore men who were only
Prophets had been called gods, how could it be a blasphemy to call oneself Son of God? From this
Maulawi Muhammad Ali concludes, and he is right in his conclusion, that Jesusas called himself 'son of God' in one sense while his enemies accused him of having claimed godhood in another sense of the word. As a matter of fact, Jesusas claimed to be god in the same sense in which the Prophets before him were called gods. As Maulawi Muhammad Ali writes on page 5 of
The Split, "He (Jesusas) says that before him those who received the word of God were called gods though they were men".
Let us now look at the case of the Promised
Messiahas. He himself says that his enemies accused him of having claimed prophethood in the sense of being the founder of a new Law. (Vide letter
Truth about the Split published in the Akhbar-e-‘Am already quoted). This charge corresponds to that which the Jews brought against Jesusas, namely that he claimed godhood in the sense of being actually the Deity or His partner, both of which were blasphemies. The Promised Messiahas denies the charge of his enemies and says that he never claimed prophethood in the sense ascribed to him by them. This corresponds to the denial of Jesusas that claimed to be 'son of God' in the sense ascribed by the Jews. Then again the Promised Messiahas adds that the meaning which his enemies assigned to the word Nabi was incorrect; because, although it is true that the Prophets who promulgated new Laws were rightly called Ambiya’, yet the word was not limited in its application to such men, but was applicable and had been actually applied to other people who promulgated no new Laws. In fact, according to the
Promised Messiahas, the word Nabi, in its true significance, did not bear any such restricted meaning.
He says, "Among the Israelites there have been several Ambiya’ to whom no Law was revealed. They only announced prophecies which they received from
God and which served to establish the truth and prestige of the Mosaic religion. It was these prophecies that entitled them to be called Ambiya’.
The same is the case with my mission. If I am not to
Truth about the Split be called a Nabi, what other distinctive word is there which will distinguish me from other recipients of
Divine revelation?" (Vide Diary published in The
Badr, dated the 5th March 1908). Similarly in Eik
Ghalati Ka Izala he writes: "Remember this for certain that for this

cards.q: Two Further Testimonies
cards.a: Dwelling on the subject of this analogy, I wish here to quote two further testimonies. One is a testimony from the author of The Split himself and the other is a testimony from the Christian Gospels. Both prove the similarity between Maulawi Muhammad…
cards.x:
Dwelling on the subject of this analogy, I wish here to quote two further testimonies. One is a testimony from the author of The Split himself and the other is a testimony from the Christian Gospels. Both prove the similarity between Maulawi Muhammad
Ali’s party and the mistaken followers of Jesusas. As for the first, it may be remembered that in December,
1909, there was held at Lahore, a public meeting at the instance of Ahmadis at Lahore, with a view to refuting some of the charges brought against Islam by a certain Christian preacher. At that meeting the present writer as well as Maulawi Muhammad Ali and
Khwaja Kamaluddin had each to deliver a lecture.
Maulawi Muhammad Ali was to speak on "The
Truth about the Split
Sublimity of Jesus as Depicted in the Quran", which was to refute the position taken by the Christian missionary that the Quran itself testified to the superiority of Jesusas over the Holy Prophetsa. I was to speak on "Salvation" and to show which of the two religions—Christianity or Islam—furnished the true teaching relating to salvation. Khwaja Kamaluddin’s topic was "A comparison of the Quran and other
Scriptures". Khwaja Kamaluddin and myself had spoken on our respective subjects before it was the turn of Maulawi Muhammad Ali, who had occasion to make some reference to the speeches of both of us. In refuting the Christian contention that the Quranic words:
went to prove the superiority of Jesusas, Maulawi
Muhammad Ali cited my personal case as an example pointing out how marvellously deep and true were the observations made by me in my lecture although I was then only 20 years of age. My age, the lecturer said, was the age of play; my address was therefore a veritable instance of the same, the lecturer continued, was the case with Jesusas. By the way, the readers may note that at that time, Maulawi
Muhammad Ali saw in me a certain resemblance to
Jesusas, although now he seems more disposed to
Truth about the Split compare me with Jesusas misguided followers. On the other hand, when making a reference to Khwaja
Kamaluddin, the words which escaped the speaker were, "as has just now been said by Khwaja
Kamaluddin, the St. Paul of our Movement". Hardly had the words been uttered when a hush fell upon the assembly, and the face of the speaker himself, as he turned towards the Khwaja betrayed a considerable amount of confusion. Maulawi Muhammad Ali will not, I believe, deny this incident to which I myself and many other people, present in the assembly, are prepared to bear sworn testimony. It was not a private discourse. It was public lecture and Providence put the words into the speaker’s mouth. Nor could it be that Khwaja Sahib was compared to St. Paul without any reason. The similarity could hardly have occurred to the speaker without a certain basis in fact. The truth was that Maulawi Muhammad Ali had at that time perceived the direction towards which Khwaja Sahib was then drifting, and the thought in his mind found unconscious expression through his lips. But unfortunately later on he himself chose to follow the same course and became ultimately the leader of the party which shared the views of Khwaja Sahib!
Truth about the Split
Mark how far thou hast drifted;
From where to where thy path has led!
To speak next of the testimony of the Christian
Scriptures, it may be noticed that according to those writings the first mistake which the disciples of
Jesusas committed after the disappearance of their
Master, was not on the question of 'Godhood' or
'sonship' of Jesusas. As a matter of fact, the Scriptures are quite innocent of that controversy. The idea of the
'God-hood' of Jesusas arose about three centuries later as a result of the conversion of the Roman Empire to
Christianity. History bears out that the doctrines of the
'Godhood' of Jesusas and of the triunal personality of the Deity were gradually introduced into Christianity through the influence of the religions then prevalent in
Europe. The first departure which the followers of
Jesusas made from his teachings was in the matter of softening the strictness of the Law and adapting it to the views of other communities with a view to inducing them to accept the new religion. As may be seen from the New Testament. Paul and Branabas had in Antioch granted certain relaxations of the Mosaic
Law to the gentile converts. But certain men who came down from Judea taught the brethren and said,
Truth about the Split
"Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved". When therefore Paul and
Baranabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas and certain other men should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question... But then rose up certain men of the sect of the Pharisees, who believed, saying that it was needful to circumcise them and to command them to keep the Law of
Mosesas. And the apostles and elders came together to consider this matter. And when there had been much disputing, all the multitude kept silence, and gave audience, Barnabas and Paul declaring what miracles and wonders God had wrought among the gentiles by them.... Then pleased it the apostles and elders with the whole Church to send chosen men of their company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. And they wrote letters by them after this manner. The apostles and elders and brethren send greetings unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and
Syria and Cilicia. For as much as we have heard that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying you must be circumcised and keep the Law, to whom we gave no such commandment. It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord to send chosen men unto
Truth about the Split you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, men that have hazarded their lives for the name of God, Lord
Jesus Christ. We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who shall also tell you the same thing by mouth. For it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things:
that you abstain from meats offered to idols and from blood and from things strangled and from fornication, from which if you keep yourselves, ye shall do well.
Fare ye well. (The Acts 15).
Maulawi Muhammad Ali and his party may now consider whether the line of action adopted by them is not the same as that followed by the early Christians.
While on the one hand in order to win the goodwill of non-Ahmadis and to secure their cooperation they professed it as highly injurious to the interest of Islam even to mention the name of the Promised Messiahas in their speeches and writings, on the other, in order to placate non-Muslims they do not hesitate even to detract from the dignity of the Holy Prophetsa himself.
For instance, it has been confessed by Khwaja
Kamaluddin that once a person wrote to him saying that he approved of everything spoken by the Khwaja except that the latter attributed to the Holy Prophetsa a rank superior to that of Jesusas. Such an attitude, the writer said, did not commend itself to him, and was an
Truth about the Split obstacle in his path. Khwaja Kamaluddin wrote in reply that the Muslims were commanded:
i.e. not to make any distinction between the
Prophetsas, and that accordingly Muslims did not attribute to any of the Prophets a rank superior to that of others. But all the while Khwaja Sahib must have been aware that the verse referred to by him did not signify what he had sought to make out of it for the benefit of his correspondent. His object in detracting from the dignity of the Holy Prophetsa was nothing else than to make his correspondent form a favourable opinion regarding Islam and to increase the number of his own converts. Further, it lies to his account that he sought to overstep the bounds of the Islamic Shariah (Law) by eating meat improperly slaughtered. He also contrived by devious means to secure from Khalifatul
Masih Ira permission to pray in England behind a non-
Ahmadi Imam. These and many other facts go to show that his general attitude was to relax as much as possible the provisions of the Islamic Law in order to win the good opinion of non-Ahmadis. They also show how close is the resemblance between the party of Maulawi Muhammad Ali and that of early
Christians. 'Then look well and ponder, O ye gifted with sight.'
Truth about the Split

cards.q: Argument from Hadith
cards.a: Muhammad Ali has adduced in support of his case a saying of the Holy Prophetsa to the effect that the…
cards.x:
Muhammad Ali has adduced in support of his case a saying of the Holy Prophetsa to the effect that the
Muslims will once follow the ways of the Jews and the Christians. Maulawi Muhammad Ali argues from this that while the general body of Muslims have played the part of the Jews by their denial of the
Promised Messiahas, it was necessary for the fulfilment of the prophecy that another section should play the part of Christians by following their ways, and it accordingly happened that after the death of the
Promised Messiahas one large party of his followers began unduly to exalt his rank. This argument does contain some truth in so far as by reason of the
Promised Messiahas being the countre-type of the first
Messiah, it was natural that some of the followers of the former should actually play the role of the followers of the latter. But that is by no means the main sense of the saying referred to. As has been explained by the Promised Messiahas himself, to be turned into Jews refers to the denial of the Promised
Messiahas, and to be turned into 'Dal' means to be actually converted to Christianity. The saying of the
Holy Prophetsa referred to by Maulawi Muhammad
Ali is in fact not a separate prophecy but simply an elucidation of one of the prophecies contained in the
Truth about the Split
Holy Quran. In the opening chapter of the Holy
Quran, God has taught the believers to pray:
"O God! lead us to the right path, the path of those on whom thou hast showered Thy favours, excepting those who have been the objects of (Thy) wrath and the misguided." This prayer contains prediction of three events which were to occur in the later history of
Islam. The first was that among Muslims there were to arise men who would be recipients of the greatest of Divine favours—including the attaining to the rank of Prophetsas. There was also to arise among them a party which was to be "the object of Divine wrath", and there was to be another section of them who were to be the Dal or the misguided. The parties referred to in the Maghdubi ‘Alaihim (objects of wrath) and the
Dal (the misguided) were described by the Holy
Prophetas himself. According to him, the first referred to the Jews and the second to the Christians. This may be seen in Tirmidhi’s collection of Hadith, where it has been narrated on the authority of Adi Ibni Hatim that the Holy Prophetsa said that the Jews were the
Maghdubi ‘Alaihim and the Christians the Dal. This interpretation by the Holy Prophetsa himself therefore leaves no doubt that the prayer contained in the
Truth about the Split opening chapter of the Holy Quran is a prayer for security from being turned into Jews and Christians.
The prediction of the Holy Prophetsa that Muslims will follow the ways of those who had gone before them, and his answer—''Of whom else?"—to the question of his Companions whether he meant that they would follow the ways of the Jews and the
Christians do not therefore make a separate prophecy, but are simply an elucidation of the prophecy already contained in the opening chapter of the Holy Quran. I shall now proceed to a discussion of the meaning of the prophecy and shall in the first place consider the interpretation given to the prophecy by the Promised
Messiahas, because the person whose advent formed the subject matter of the prophecy was certainly the most competent authority to furnish a correct interpretation of the same. After that I shall go on to consider the meaning of the Holy Prophet’s saying from the point of view of mere common sense.
The Promised Messiahas writes on page 63 of the
Tuhfa’-e-Golarhwiyyah: "Only two dangers have been mentioned. The one is internal viz. acting like the
Jews and persecuting the Promised Messiahas, and the second external, viz. conversion to Christianity. You ought to know and remember well that in the opening chapter of the Holy Quran, the dangers against which
Truth about the Split
Muslims have been taught to pray for protection are only two in number, viz. (1) to deem him an infidel who was to arise as the Messiahas in Islam—to bring him into contempt, to seek to cast aspersions upon his character, to pronounce the fatwa of death against him. These are the dangers referred to in the verse
"Ghairil Maghdubi ‘Alaihim". (2) The second danger against which the Muslims have been taught to seek protection in the chapter, is the danger of Christianity and the fact that the chapter closes with the mention of this danger indicates that the danger of Christianity will be like a mighty flood and will surpass every other danger."
This interpretation by the Promised Messiahas— that by being turned into Jews what was signified was antagonism to the Promised Messiahas, and that by being turned into Christians was meant actual conversion to Christianity of many of the Muslims of his time and not that his own followers would act the role of the Christians—ought to have been conclusive for every
Ahmadi.
Nevertheless,
Maulawi
Muhammad Ali chose to put a new interpretation on the prophecy and on the Quranic verse. Such an attitude on his part will hardly come as a surprise to those who during the last four years have observed his gradual lapse from loyalty to his Master, but it cannot
Truth about the Split fail to strike those before whom the Maulawi Sahib has appeared for the first time in his new role.
Next, when we consider the prophecy in the light of actual events, we may notice that even from the point of view of common sense, the interpretation given by the Promised Messiahas is the only one which can be deemed valid and correct. The Holy
Prophetsa had prophesied that Muslims would come to resemble Jews and Christians. We may notice that in religious matters the only likeness to the Jews which
Muslims have acquired is that, like Jews, Muslims at large have denied the Messiah who appeared among them. They have not indeed adopted any of the peculiarities which distinguish Judaism from other faiths; nor has any considerable party of them actually joined the rank of the Jews who, it maybe noted, are as a rule reluctant to admit strangers into their community. Therefore, to be the like of Jews clearly signified, in the case of Muslims, denial of their
Messiah and antagonism to him. But, on the other hand, "following the ways of the Christians" can justly be interpreted as actual conversion to
Christianity; for, as a matter of fact we find that at the present time all the Muslim sects with the solitary exception of the
Ahmadiyya
Community are unanimous in unduly magnifying the dignity of Jesusas
Truth about the Split and in according to him a rank superior to that of the
Holy Prophetsa. For it is a patent fact that the Muslims have been so deeply imbued with the doctrines of
Christianity that while they admit that their own
Prophet is dead and lies buried in an earthly grave, they believe that Jesus is still alive residing in the heavens. They thus corroborate the divinity of Jesusas by attributing to him a kind of living and eternal existence. Further, they entertain the belief that Jesus like the Almighty God was a quickener of the dead.
Such opinions do in fact make the Muslims the counter-types of Christians, because in strange contrast with such beliefs regarding Jesus, we may note that Muslim theologians do not admit regarding their own Prophet that he infused life even into a single bird. Thus these Muslims do in a way surpass the Christians in attributing to Jesus the power of creation. They also believe that Jesus possessed knowledge of the unseen, so much so, that knowledge of the last day, universally regarded as a special prerogative of God was, according to them, another of the peculiarities possessed by Jesusas. In view of such a similarity of beliefs, there is little room for doubt that present-day Muslims have become virtually like
Christians. The latter represent one of the most actively proselytizing peoples of the world, and have
Truth about the Split by this time already converted several millions of
Muslims to their faith. All these facts are clear and palpable as the day; but still to close one’s eyes to them and—contrary to the views of the Promised
Messiahas—to seek to discover the like of Christians among his own followers is, to say the least, highly unfair and improper on the part of one who still professes to be ones of his disciples.

cards.q: The Two Messiahs Contrasted
cards.a: It is no doubt true that as a necessary corollary of the fact that the Promised Messiahas was a counter- type of Jesusas, a certain number of the former’s followers like those of the latter were destined to deviate from the right path, but that event is not obviously what is referred to in the prophecy we now have under consideration.
