cards.q: "If Jesus could be born miraculously, why can't he come down from the sky as a second miracle?"
cards.a: Everything is possible for Allah — the question is whether He did it. The Quran answers about the birth: Jesus is like Adam, who had neither father nor mother. But raising a body to heaven is against Allah's practice (sunnah), and the Quran never says it. The verse "bal rafa'ahullahu ilaihi" means Allah raised him towards Himself — in nearness and rank, since Allah has no direction.
cards.x:
Huzoor (rh) recalled a maulvi who asked him why Jesus cannot go to heaven if God is All-Powerful. He replied: then why can't he go to Kashmir? God has power over everything; the question is what He actually did, and the Quran shows His practice.

In the prayer between the two prostrations, every Muslim says "warfa'ni" — raise me. If rafa meant lifting the body, we would be asking to be carried up to the sky in the middle of prayer. A hadith says that the more a servant humbles himself before Allah, the higher Allah raises him, even to the seventh heaven. So wherever the Quran and Hadith speak of Allah raising a servant, it means nearness to Him. Jesus was raised to Allah — and Allah is everywhere, so "towards Allah" cannot mean a physical direction.
cards.pg: Majalis-e-Irfan, pp. 106–112

cards.q: "I am sometimes Adam, sometimes Moses, sometimes Jacob" — does this couplet raise him above the prophets?
cards.a: No. The Promised Messiah (as) was sent as a servant of the Holy Prophet (sa) to show that the servant of Muhammad (sa) is greater than those who claim to be God's son. The Quran foretold a time when "the messengers are gathered together" (77:12): all the earlier prophets' promised returns are fulfilled in one person of this Ummah.
cards.x:
Huzoor (rh) explained that the followers of every faith await the return of their founder — Krishna, Buddha and others — and the signs of the Mahdi given by the Holy Prophet (sa) match them all. Logically there were two possibilities: each prophet appears in his own nation, which would break Islam into pieces; or one person in the Ummah of Muhammad (sa) represents them all. The second is what happened.

A Shia Imam wrote that when the Mahdi comes he will say: I am Adam, I am Moses, I am Abraham — and I am the true copy of the Holy Prophet (sa). This shows that all the prophets take pride in being servants of the Holy Prophet (sa). The couplet expresses exactly this, not superiority over anyone.
cards.pg: Majalis-e-Irfan, pp. 120–122

cards.q: Will Mujaddids keep coming every century?
cards.a: Mujaddidiyyat stood in place of Khilafat. Khilafat-e-Rashida ended early, so Allah raised Mujaddids to keep Islam alive. But the Holy Prophet (sa) foretold that after the Messiah, "Khilafat on the precept of prophethood" would return — so after the Promised Messiah (as) the Khilafat continues, and a separate Mujaddid is no longer needed. If needed, Allah can give a Khalifa the work of a Mujaddid.
cards.x:
Huzoor (rh) explained that a Mujaddid is not mentioned in the Quran, which speaks of Khilafat. When Khilafat broke and Islam split, Allah raised Mujaddids such as Umar bin Abdul Aziz. As the Muslim world spread, several Mujaddids appeared at once in different lands, and many never even claimed the title.

If Mujaddids kept appearing alongside a living Khilafat, they would divide the community instead of uniting it. That is why the Holy Prophet (sa), after foretelling Mujaddids, also said: "Then there will be Khilafat on the precept of prophethood" (Musnad Ahmad). While Khilafat continues, Allah can grant any Khalifa the special ability of renewal.
cards.pg: Majalis-e-Irfan, pp. 122–124

cards.q: "How can you say everyone buried in Bahishti Maqbara is in paradise?"
cards.a: No one except Allah can make anyone dwell in paradise. Ahmadis do not believe that burial in Bahishti Maqbara is a certificate of paradise. The Promised Messiah (as) received the glad tidings that those who join the system of Wasiyyat with full sincerity and keep its conditions are people of paradise — even those who could not be buried there.
cards.x:
Huzoor (rh) said exaggeration in anything does harm. If people thought the committee issuing a burial permit was issuing a passport to paradise, that would be wrong. Bahishti Maqbara is the one established by Allah's decree; but a person may deceive people and get in, yet he cannot deceive God.

Ahmadis only say: we have a good opinion of God. For a person who sacrificed his whole life, we hope Allah will forgive him and that he will enter paradise. But no human — whatever his rank — can make anyone dwell in paradise unless God informs him.
